:::{#exm-outer-product-matvec}
#### Multiplying an outer product by a vector

Take $\vecf{u} = (1, 2, 3)$ and $\vecf{v} = (4, 5)$
from [the example of an outer product](#exm-outer-product),
and $\vecf{w} = (1, -1)$.
[Multiplying](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matvec-mult) the [outer product](#def-outer-product) by $\vecf{w}$ directly gives

$$
\ba
\paren{\oprod{\vecf{u}}{\vecf{v}}} \vecf{w}
&= \begin{bmatrix}
4 & 5 \\
8 & 10 \\
12 & 15
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(the outer product found in that example)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix}
4 - 5 \\
8 - 10 \\
12 - 15
\end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(definition of matrix-vector multiplication)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ -2 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

The [dot product](linear-algebra.qmd#def-dot-product) of $\vecf{v}$ and $\vecf{w}$ is

$$
\ba
\tprod{\vecf{v}}{\vecf{w}}
&= 4 \cd 1 + 5 \cd (-1)
&& \text{(definition of the dot product)}
\\
&= -1
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

and $(-1)\,\vecf{u} = (-1, -2, -3)$ is the same vector,
as @thm-outer-product-matvec says.
